#1322. Gasperini: ‘Roma will learn more from Man Utd defeat than Real Madrid’

Gian Piero Gasperini insists Roma ‘will learn’ from their Champions League collapse at Manchester United, more so than when doing the same with Real Madrid. ‘Disappointment sets in.’

This is evidently now a pattern for the Giallorossi, not just in the Champions League with the 3-1 advantage fumbled against Real Madrid in seven minutes, but in Serie A too when caught for draws after going in front.

They were in control at Old Trafford, leading 2-0 after 18 minutes with Matias Soulé and the Donyell Malen penalty, with several opportunities to score a third.

However, once Bruno Fernandes converted a soft spot-kick, which was first saved by Devis Vasquez only to be retaken for encroachment, it was a different match, and Matheus Cunha’s late double secured the first Manchester United victory since September 10.

“It was a different game to Real Madrid, where it all happened in the last seven or eight minutes from corner kicks, and there were no real signs of the comeback,” Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia.

“This time, it was above all after the penalty that Manchester United had this sudden surge of enthusiasm, and we were unable to keep up with it.”

Considering it happened twice in the last three Champions League games, it cannot be a coincidence that Roma crumble when leading.

“I don’t think it’s a coincidence, but I also think they were different matches. This evening, we didn’t have the strength to press their strikers the way we did in the first half, plus the penalty and the error for the equaliser really turned the tide.

“There is always going to be 15-20 minutes against Manchester United when you’re under pressure, and if you can emerge unscathed from it, you’ll be fine.”

The defeat to Real Madrid was dominated for longer, yet because of the calibre of opponent, it feels as if this loss to Manchester United hurts more for Roma because it was such a wasted opportunity.

“Honestly, we learned more from this match than the one with Real Madrid. That felt unpredictable, whereas at times today when Old Trafford was pushing on the team, we need to be able to handle these situations better in future,” conceded Gasperini.

“They made modifications at half-time and had nothing left to lose, so they pressed high, so perhaps we should’ve made more of long balls in that situation. The problem was we were no longer able to stick to their reference points, so they had the better on pressing, not letting us play, but also on their attacks. That created some problems for us, we probably should’ve tried to interrupt their rhythm a bit more with some extra challenges and slow the tempo down.

“The momentum of the match changed with the penalty and the incident for 2-2.”

Another recurring mistake Roma are guilty of is crumbling the moment something goes wrong, as within 60 seconds of the Bruno Fernandes penalty, Bryan Mbeumo hit the woodwork, and three minutes after the equaliser was the winning goal.

“That’s true, it happened against Real Madrid too, so perhaps there is a bit of disappointment that sets in when you see the victory drifting away. Again, we need the team to take the pressure of a result at all costs off itself, so this game will help us learn more than others,” confirmed Gasperini.

It was not the best build-up to this match, seeing as both Mile Svilar and Pierluigi Gollini were ruled out by injury, so Vasquez had to make his club debut as third-choice shot-stopper.

Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné and Lorenzo Pellegrini were also out, and Devyne Rensch limped off with a muscular issue in the first half, but Nahuel Molina wasn’t introduced.

“Molina is an international, but Rensch started very well and had this injury, so I chose Lulli and that used up a slot. Wesley played well defensively, this was not the reason we struggled.”

#1321. The brain liquidates billions of mutant neurons around the time we’re born

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

By the time a baby is born, its brain has lost large numbers of neurons with genetic abnormalities.Credit: Getty

Around the time of birth, the developing human brain mysteriously tidies up by purging itself of a vast number of mutation-riddled neurons, according to a painstaking analysis of more than 2,300 nerve cells.

We are all mosaics: vast genetic diversity found between cells in a single person

We are all mosaics: vast genetic diversity found between cells in a single person

The analysis, published in Nature1 on 28 October, found that more than one-quarter of the sampled neurons from the brains of human fetuses had either gained or lost several segments of their chromosomes. By contrast, only about 6% of neurons from the brains of babies after birth had such abnormalities. “It suggests that the neurons that survive may be the ones that have kept the most intact genomes during development,” says Christos Proukakis, a neurologist at University College London, who was not involved in the study.

The findings reveal a new mechanism for regulating how many neurons a person has and for deciding which fetal neurons are allowed to persist in the brain, says Diane Shao, a paediatric neurogeneticist at Boston Children’s Hospital in Massachusetts and first author on the paper.

Learning more about this process could be key to understanding neurological conditions that often appear in childhood, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and epilepsy.

Studies in mice2 have suggested that, during early development, mammals eliminate many brain cells by activating a molecular programme that leads to the cells’ deaths. Shao and her colleagues analysed human brain development by studying the brains of deceased individuals ranging from fetuses at 14 weeks of gestation to nonagenarians. The team focused on neurons in the cerebral cortex, a region of the brain responsible for memory, learning and consciousness, among other functions.

How to make a brain: new experiments challenge existing picture

How to make a brain: new experiments challenge existing picture

The team analysed the genomes of individual neurons to look for those that had either lost or gained some chromosomal segments, a phenomenon called copy number variation. The analysis revealed that a stunning number of cells with widespread copy number variation were present during fetal development. There were so many that Shao and her colleagues spent years trying to work out whether the results were real. But even after repeating the experiment using a different single-cell sequencing method, the results were similar.

After birth, however, the proportion of these abnormal neurons dropped by more than fourfold, suggesting that they had been culled during development.

How does the brain know which neurons are normal and which are not? One possible clue, says Shao, is that those brain cells with high levels of copy number variation also tended to show abnormal activity of genes involved in forming connections, or synapses, with other neurons.

#1320. Pocognoli backs returning star McTominay to lead Scotland into new era

Published: 15:09 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:55 EDT, 3 November 2026

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli has welcomed Scott McTominay back into the fold after heart surgery and revealed he’s banking on him to help kickstart a new era for the national team.

McTominay went through a minor operation to address mild benign arrhythmia in September and missed Pocognoli’s first Nations League camp as head coach.

However, having scored four times after returning to action at Italian outfit Napoli, the 29-year-old midfielder is back in the squad for this month’s double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Torino striker Che Adams, absent last time out due to a muscle strain, is also back in the fold while there is a first call-up for left-back James Penrice, currently on loan at Rangers from Greek side AEK Athens.

Celtic left-back Kieran Tierney returns after withdrawing from Pocognoli’s first squad while centre-back Scott McKenna misses out after reportedly picking up a back strain playing for Dinamo Zagreb. Josh Doig, Colby Donovan, James Wilson and Lennon Miller also drop out from Pocognoli’s debut matches.

Scott McTominay is fit and available for Scotland after minor heart surgery

Speaking while naming his squad at Hampden Park, Pocognoli emphasised the role McTominay will play – along with other senior stars – in helping bring through a new generation of stars under his guidance.

‘I have been in contact with Scott from the first day. He missed the first camp with some physical problem,’ stated the Belgian.

‘We were still in contact during the rehabilitation, when he came back on the pitch. He’s one of the captains, so there’s a special contact with them, but he’s looking forward to come, to play for us, to play in a different way, on the pitch and he is very positive, so that’s important.

‘There is plenty of experience back in the squad. With Scott, with Che, with Kieran. He’s also back, so, if you accumulate the caps, we have some experience that will be useful for this camp and to also embrace the young lads - because we still have a young squad with many players who don’t have a lot of caps.

‘I’m sure the mix will be good and these (experienced) players will also show the way for them.’

Sebastien Pocognoli has picked his squad to face North Macedonia and Switzerland

Scotland are third in Group B1 with four points from four games, three points behind Slovenia and eight behind runaway leaders Switzerland. The Scots host North Macedonia at Hampden on November 13 with a trip to Switzerland three days later.

With one eye on the forthcoming 2028 European Championship qualifying campaign, Pocognoli said: ‘I’m looking forward to working with everybody, but, for sure, we want to see most of the players just to have as much information as possible to start the qualification for the Euros.

‘All I want to do now is to get the most out of this, to know my squad as deeply as possible, to see the body language, the attitude of the players in some situations, and to have most of the information to start the big job.’

On the issue of a first call-up for 27-year-old former Hearts defender Penrice, Pocognoli said: ‘Like I said in the first camp, we have a list of players that we select regarding the performance at their clubs, but also the style of play or the way that we want to play.

‘We have some missing players around the left side, so, combined with his quality and what we are looking for on the pitch, it’s a logical choice for me. It can be very useful for the system that we want to play and also I think he deserves it.’

Lamine Yamal has been criticised by Spanish journalist Pedro Martin following the tragic death of Tenerife footballer, Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital on Monday after a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Segunda Division clash.

The Spaniard went into cardiac arrest after suffering neck and head injuries. Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned amid serious concern for De Miguel.

De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday. However, his health took a turn for the worse, and he sadly lost his life on Tuesday morning.

"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true," Tenerife said in a statement. "There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today."

Barcelona welcomed Aston Villa to Camp Nou for their Champions League clash on Tuesday evening. The La Liga giants ran out 3-0 victors thanks to goals from Yamal and Raphinha (2).

Yamal opened the scoring in the seventh minute as he capatalised on a mistake from Joao Gomes. The 19-year-old had a beaming smile on his face as he celebrated his goal by the corner flag.

Martin was not impressed with Yamal's actions following the goal. The COPE journalist believes he should have dedicated his goal to De Miguel following his tragic death. He said:

"It wouldn't have been a bad idea for Lamine Yamal to remember the Tenerife player, but he must be focused on his own things."

Martin's comments have not gone down well. 'What a disgusting and miserable human', one fan wrote.

A second said: 'I sincerely believe that it’s unnecessary to say this. Lamine Yamal doesn’t have to celebrate by dedicating the goal to Jesús de Miguel; that doesn’t mean he doesn’t remember him. Memory deserves respect, but it shouldn’t be used to hold a kid accountable for how he celebrates a goal.'

A third wrote: 'How miserable do you have to be to use the death of a 30-year-old player to attack one you don't like.'

While a fourth commented: 'It seems lamentable to me to use the death of a fellow professional of Lamine Yamal to throw s*** at him. You have no shame.'

Raphina looked more subdued after each of his two goals. He paid tribute to De Miguel after the match.

"Sorry, tonight I don’t want to talk about football. It’s clear that I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but I want to send a lot of strength to Jesus de Miguel’s family," he said.

“May he rest in peace. In the end, this can happen to anyone. The truth is that it’s very tough... when we saw the news this morning, it was complicated. I’m incredibly shocked and sad.

“In the end, you go to play a match, and the same thing could happen to you. From myself, from the club, we want to send a lot of strength to his family.”

Barcelona return to La Liga action on Sunday evening when they travel to the Wanda Metropolitano to take on Atletico Madrid.

#1318. Chivu: ‘Inter were the best version of ourselves’ in 3-0 victory at Feyenoord

Cristian Chivu feels Inter were ‘the best version of ourselves’ in tonight’s 3-0 Champions League victory away to Feyenoord, but ‘consistency is what brings results.’

The Nerazzurri were under pressure in Rotterdam and needed to send a response after their 3-1 defeat to Milan in the Derby della Madonnina on Saturday.

It was certainly that, as they dominated against a Feyenoord side that beat Como here 3-2 and has a notoriously strong home record.

Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski were all on target in a pretty comfortable encounter, and Esposito had another goal ruled inches offside on a Federico Dimarco pass.

Notably, Inter have been criticised for their bad starts to games and it was not since August that they had scored in the opening eight minutes.

“We have certain values, we understood certain things and put them on the pitch,” Chivu told Sky Sport Italia.

“That doesn’t mean we haven’t done well so far this season. We tried to be the best version of ourselves, it worked today with organisation, intensity and everything we needed for a strong performance in a stadium that is not easy to play in.”

What did the coach mean when saying the team understood certain things?

“We always have discussions after every game, whether it goes well or badly, we try to correct errors and build on our strengths. Sometimes it goes better than others, perhaps we understood what wasn’t going as well,” said Chivu.

“The Inter world, the club owners, the fans, we are all aware of the values of these players who want to fly the flag high, that has never been in doubt.”

Another recurring problem so far this season has been a lack of consistency throughout the 90 minutes, but this evening they always seemed to be in control.

“Consistency is what brings results, it gives you self-confidence and belief in what you are doing, it is what we are looking for at this moment. This game gives us a big boost of confidence in what we are building, so we know football can take you down some strange paths, but you must be able to react and get back onto the right path,” concluded the Inter coach.

This result allows Inter to climb up the Champions League table, but they still have only six points from four games, so it will be a fight to the end in order to scrape into the next round.

A team like inter with all talents is struggling to win a match, beating Fayenoord looks like lifting UCL cup,wake up and do more compete with Europe’s best teams because you have all it takes

Anybody who saw the match could see how Inter dominated Feyernoord thanks to the whole team pressing high, aggressive attitude from the start.

Milan stand no chance when this is the mindset!

#1317. Mikel Arteta reveals Arsenal have a 'massive library' of videos showing rivals pulling shirts - as he hits back after Alexander Isak controversy

Published: 15:50 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 16:22 EDT, 3 November 2026

Mikel Arteta has revealed he has a ‘massive library’ of video footage showing other teams pulling shirts - having last month disclosed he is keeping a similar dossier of other Premier League managers leaving their technical area.

Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber escaped punishment for making contact with Alexander Isak in Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday.

Timber tugged Isak’s shirt as the striker went to head the ball towards goal, but referee Andy Madley did not award a foul and VAR decided against recommending an on-field review. The decision has since been widely scrutinised.

When asked if there is now a danger referees will change tack and give penalties for and free-kicks for the offence, Arteta said: ‘Yeah, I have a lot of clips about shirt pulls and grabs.

‘I have a massive library that we can talk about. I have a massive library that we can (put out) there to remind everybody what every team is going through.’

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola and captain Virgil van Dijk were outraged when they weren't awarded a penalty after Jurrien Timber pulled back Alexander Isak

Now Mikel Arteta has claimed he is keeping a dossier of similar incidents of shirt pulling which has gone unpunished

Last month Arteta claimed his touchline behaviour is punished far more harshly than that of other Premier League managers and said he had clips of his counterparts breaching their own technical areas as evidence.

‘I do have to be careful, and we need to have good sensors there,’ Arteta said after being booked during Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton.

‘There are managers that have the record in the league - 36 times in 10 minutes leaving the touchline, no yellows.

‘So I'm clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. So if somebody is going to say, “I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record”, then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the (other) manager.

Arteta also revealed William Saliba is ready to make his first appearance since sustaining a back injury in July as he pushes to feature against Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

Saliba played 45 minutes in behind-closed-doors friendly last week and was part of Arsenal’s travelling squad for their Champions League fixture in Prague.

The 25-year-old also took part in full training this morning for the first time since picking up a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain in July.

Arsenal have coped well without him, with summer signing Ezri Konsa forming an impressive partnership with Gabriel. The Gunners have conceded only five goals in nine Premier League games, which is the best defensive record in the division.

William Saliba is back in contention for the Gunners after missing the start of the season with a back injury sustained at the World Cup

Arteta said: ‘He's in a really good place. I think the timings and the manner that the injury has been dealt with, and especially the feelings that Willy has been having along the way, have been very, very positive.

‘He feels very comfortable, he played 45 minutes behind closed doors last week and he feels ready to go. So whether we use him or not now is a matter of what the team needs.

‘All the preparation has been done to measure all the loads and minimise the risk. Now he's in a really good place, he's built the capacity that we needed and now it's about giving him minutes.’

On how eager Saliba is to play, he added: ‘I think he's very desperate and very loved, because William is somebody that is admired and very liked around the team.

‘Every time he's around, he creates something special. That's William, that's his nature. He's around the team now, and we need to give him the right moment, the right amount of minutes, and hopefully that's going to be very soon.’

#1316. Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola said: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1315. Champions League Icon Looks Unrecognisable, 13 Years After Retiring

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Many wonderful footballers have lit up the Champions League since the tournament was rebranded from the European Cup in 1992.

While Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, two of the greatest football players of all time, are the icons who’ll immediately spring to mind for many football fans, we can’t overlook the likes of Luka Modric, Xavi and Andres Iniesta, Zinedine Zidane, Paolo Maldini, Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale, Raul, Clarence Seedorf… the list goes on and on.

Then you have the cult heroes. The ‘Streets Will Never Forget’ players who will always occupy a special place in the hearts of football fans who watched Champions League matches in the 1990s and 2000s.

We’re talking Adriano. We’re talking Gabriel Batistuta. We’re talking Juan Carlos Valeron, Rustu Recber and Joan Roman Riquelme.

Another player who falls into this category is arguably the greatest free-kick taker in football history. If you know, you know.

Messi has netted an astonishing 76 free-kicks over the course of his glittering career, at the time of writing, but that still only puts the Argentine legend second on that particular list.

The free-kick GOAT with 77 scored is currently Juninho Pernambucano, who banged in some of the most outrageous set-piece goals we’ll ever see on a football pitch.

Best remembered for his eight-year spell with French side Lyon between 2001 and 2009, scoring 100 goals in 343 appearances, Juninho also earned 40 caps for the Brazilian national team.

Many of his goals for Lyon were long-range ‘knuckle-ball’ free-kicks, which deceived even the world’s best goalkeepers, such as Bayern Munich’s Oliver Kahn.

“Much like King Arthur had Excalibur and William Tell his crossbow, the folk hero Juninho possessed his own special weapon to save the day - his legendary free-kicks,” journalist Carl Anka wrote for BBC Sport in 2018.

“No one hit a free-kick quite like Juninho. No one. At a time when most footballers either opted for a refined instep 'up and over' technique a la David Beckham or Zinedine Zidane, or the thunderous 'hit it and hope' stylings of Roberto Carlos, Juninho did something else entirely. He did everything.”

Juninho retired in 2013 following a third and final spell with Brazilian outfit Vasco da Gama. He worked as a football commentator for Brazilian sports network Rede Globo before becoming Lyon’s sporting director in 2019.

He stepped down two years later, following a mixed spell in charge, before being linked with a return in 2023.

But Juninho appears to be enjoying retirement with his family for the time being - although many football fans wouldn’t even recognise him these days if they passed him in the street.

Juninho still has the long’ish hair, although it’s now turned silver. The 51-year-old, who is now a grandfather, sports an impressive grey beard and wears glasses.

Away from football, Juninho has used his celebrity status to speak out against systemic racism and police violence in Brazil.

#1314. Oxlade-Chamberlain isn't the first big name to flop in Scotland... Five superstars who failed to make their mark in the Scottish top-flight

Published: 15:47 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 16:34 EDT, 3 November 2026

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's inability to nail down a starting slot in a struggling Celtic side has reinforced the theory that the hard and physical Scottish Premiership is not exactly a place for former English Premier League stars to head to in their twilight years with a view to coasting through to retirement.

Oxlade-Chamberlain arrived at Parkhead back in January with a sparkling CV that boasted a full house of domestic trophies in England plus a Champions League win and 35 international caps from spells at Southampton, Arsenal and Liverpool.

The 33-year-old has been unable to nail down a regular spot at Celtic Park, though, and was given a rare start at the weekend in the champions’ 2-0 loss away to Falkirk.

Here, in a Daily Mail Sport special, we look at five other big-name stars who have failed in Scotland in the wake of enjoying successful careers south of the border.

Arsenal legend Wright’s best days were long behind him when then Celtic manager John Barnes brought him in as a replacement for the injured Henrik Larsson up front during the 1999-2000 season.

Wright had been a sensation during his seven years at the Gunners, winning a full house of domestic trophies plus a European Cup-Winners’ Cup, but he’d been on loan at Nottingham Forest from West Ham before heading for Glasgow and was clearly over the hill at the age of 35.

He made 10 appearances in total during a short-lived spell that involved a 4-2 Old Firm loss and that infamous 3-1 Scottish Cup loss to Inverness Caledonian Thistle that led to Barnes’ departure.

Wright also left soon after for Burnley and admitted the entire affair left a mark.

He told the BBC: ‘I felt I was caught up in a war crisis in Kosovo not involved in a football result that wrecked John Barnes' career as Celtic manager.

'Some so-called fans, a few morons who know nothing better, covered my car in spit. They were shouting obscenities at myself and Regi Blinker.’

The former England midfielder had carved his reputation in the English Premier League during stays at Manchester City, Newcastle United and Queens Park Rangers and arrived at Rangers in September 2016 on a two-year deal after inspiring Burnley to promotion from the Championship.

His time in Glasgow, however, proved to be a short-lived train wreck. He left in the wake of having his contract cancelled after eight games and 133 days.

English midfielder Joey Barton did not impress in his short spell at Rangers

Barton arrived, aged 34, blowing his own trumpet and aiming verbal volleys at then Celtic’s Scott Brown, but his stay very quickly unravelled and involved a 5-1 Old Firm humbling in the east end of Glasgow in which he was targeted by the Parkhead midfielder.

In the aftermath, a training-ground bust-up involving Andy Halliday saw Barton told to stay away from Rangers by manager Mark Warburton and later hit with a three-week suspension.

It was the beginning of the end. His contract was cancelled in November.

The controversial Dane had earned a move to Spanish giants Real Madrid following five great years at Everton and arrived at Celtic from the Bernabeu on a three-year contract in August 2006 on a fee said to be in the region of £2million.

Gravesen did score a couple of goals against Rangers during his time in Glasgow, but never delivered the kind of performances required and failed to hold down a regular spot in the side by the end.

Thomas Gravesen was unimpressive at Celtic and clashed with manager Gordon Strachan

He played just 22 times before returning to Everton on a loan deal in August 2007. When the Goodison outfit refused to extend that arrangement, an agreement was struck to release him from his deal at Parkhead and he duly retired from playing.

Gravesen was hugely critical of then manager Gordon Strachan in later interviews.

‘Unfortunately, I ran into an opposition to myself in the form of a coach called Gordon Strachan. It did not work between him and me,’ he said.

‘Gordon was a defensively-minded coach of a world famous club. I could not understand why he did as he did at Celtic because we were so much better than the other teams. He was nervous about losing.’

The Welshman had won three FA Cups during a spell at Arsenal in addition to a Serie A title with Juventus when arriving on loan at Rangers from the Italian outfit in January 2022.

Rangers’ then sporting director Ross Wilson was quick to publicise his role in pulling the deal together and insisted it had sent a ripple of excitement through the dressing room at the Ibrox outfit.

However, Ramsey was unable to live up to expectations during the 13 appearances he made and was often battling fitness issues. He will be forever remembered for missing the decisive penalty-kick in the Europa League final shoot-out against Germans Eintracht Frankfurt in Seville after being sent on as a substitute by boss Giovanni van Bronckhorst late in extra-time.

Ramsey missed a penalty in Europa League final

Ramsey later told Four Four Two magazine: ‘I just wish that I’d played longer in the final. I felt I could have brought something different to the table had I come on a bit earlier.

‘I was essentially brought on solely to take a penalty in the shoot-out, which I’m not sure is the best idea. That played on my mind as I went to take it, instead of being clear about where I wanted to put it. I’m still gutted that I missed that penalty and gutted for the fans that we couldn’t lift the trophy for them.

'I was really excited to go to Rangers. I had a couple of injuries during my time there, which made it difficult to get into any kind of rhythm. I [also] had a horrible case of Covid shortly before I signed, which meant I didn’t arrive in the best shape and it was no surprise that my body broke down.’

The little midfielder had won the World Cup with Brazil before arriving at Celtic in 2004. He had become a legend at Middlesbrough, where he had three spells as a player.

He’d been the subject of a £13million move to Atletico Madrid following his first spell in England and there remains a theory that he never quite recovered from a broken leg suffered in Spain in a match against Celta Vigo.

Juninho actually started well at Parkhead by stepping into the heat of an Old Firm derby and delivering a fine display as Martin O’Neill’s side recorded a one-goal win.

Celtic fans did not see the best of Juninho

However, it quickly became clear he was a shadow of his former self and quickly slid onto the substitutes’ bench under O’Neill. By January, it had become clear he just wasn’t settling in and an agreement was made to release him from his contract after seven months and just 14 starts.

‘It was an awkward situation, and an especially frustrating one for me,’ recalled Juninho in later years.

‘I ended up in Scotland, but things didn’t really work out for me. I had this issue with Martin O’Neill and his tactics. I still can’t understand why he wanted me at Celtic. He used to play with a 4-4-2 and he asked me to play out wide with defensive responsibilities, but this was never my style. It didn’t suit me and he knew it.

‘Maybe inside his head, he wasn’t looking for the Juninho of the 90s and maybe I’m to blame for that, but a manager should know a player’s style.’

Bruno Fernandes explained what went through his mind when retaking that penalty to revive Manchester United with Roma. ‘I was lucky honestly, but the second time I made a decision.’

#1312. 20 Greatest Players in Real Madrid History [Ranked]

Throughout the majority of football history, Real Madrid have been one of the best teams in the world. Their excellence over the years is almost hard to believe as they've consistently adapted with the times and kept hold of their status as one of the biggest clubs on the planet.

It's easy to see how they've managed it, though, when you take a look at the sheer calibre of players who have played for Los Blancos throughout their history.

Some of the best footballers of all time have, at one point or another, called the Bernabeu their home.

Considering just how many greats there have been at the club over the years, coming up with a list of the 20 best Real Madrid players ever is a very difficult task.

Indeed, even in this current era, the likes of Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr will all be hoping of etching their name into folklore and joining some of the club's greatest ever players.

Greatest Players in Real Madrid History 20-11

Despite impressing at Tottenham Hotspur, few could have predicted the impact that Luka Modric would have at the Santiago Bernabeu. The Croatian arrived in Spain in 2012 and had a poor first campaign as he was infamously named La Liga's worst signing of the season.

He kept working hard and went on to prove his doubters wrong as he won an unprecedented amount of silverware with Los Blancos. Over the course of 597 games, Modric lifted 28 trophies and is the most decorated player in the club's history. Considering some of the figures that they've had on the books over the years, that's quite the achievement.

One of the most exceptional strikers the sport has ever seen. Puskas netted 242 goals in 262 games in a Real Madrid shirt, an average of 0.92 per appearance. He also won three European Cups and notably scored four goals in the 7-3 final victory over Eintracht Frankfurt in 1960, the only time that feat has been achieved.

The forward even has an award named after him, the FIFA Puskas Award, given to the footballer who is deemed to have scored the most aesthetically pleasing goal over the course of 12 months. If that doesn't give you an indication of how special he was, not much would.

A man who is in the conversation to be labelled the greatest left winger in history. As well as tormenting opposing defenders for fun in a Real Madrid shirt, Gento won six (yes, SIX) European Cups, which is still the most by any footballer. He spent 18 years at the La Liga club, and played over 500 games for them.

Gento also won 12 La Liga titles, another record. There's simply no denying just how impressive he was, and he played a huge role in making the Real Madrid side he was a part of, one of the best iterations in the club's illustrious career.

The stadium is named after Bernabeu and without him, the club wouldn't be the same as it is today. He was a brilliant player in the 1920s and was then president for 35 years between 1943 and 1978, overseeing a ridiculous amount of on-pitch success. Arguably the most important figure in Real Madrid's illustrious history.

It stands to reason that the club wouldn't have grown into the behemoth that it did if it wasn't for Bernabeu's impact. Despite spending a year with the club's local rivals, Atletico Madrid, he's still regarded as an icon at Los Blancos and his legacy will never be forgotten, regardless of his limited appearances.

Santiago Bernabeu's Real Madrid Statistics

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: In 1955, Real Madrid changed the name of their stadium to Santiago Bernabeu, paying tribute to their former player and long-time president.

What a striker Raul was. He's Real Madrid's second-highest scorer with 323 goals and leads the way for appearances with an enormous 741. Raul brought an end to his incredible 16-year career at Los Blancos in 2010, with six La Liga titles and three Champions Leagues to boot.

The Champions League Golden Boot is widely seen as one of the greatest individual awards each season.

He consistently put up absurd scoring numbers throughout the majority of his career in Spain, and there were just two years during his time at the Bernabeu that he didn't score in double figures. If it wasn't for a certain Portuguese superstar, he'd still possess the top-scoring records for Madrid in the league and in the Champions League.

San Iker could do it all between the sticks and rarely ever dropped a bad performance. He's still the youngest goalkeeper to appear in a Champions League final and holds the record for the most clean sheets in the competition's history. It's a real shame things turned slightly sour towards the end of his Real Madrid career, but the fact remains that he's an all-time great.

He spent 16 years in the club's senior team and was one of the best goalkeepers in the world during his prime at the Bernabeu. Casillas won just about everything there was to win with Madrid and played over 700 times along the way. Just a world-class goalkeeper.

Probably the finest-ever Real Madrid captain. As well as leading the team marvellously for so many years and winning 22 trophies overall, Sergio Ramos scored a ridiculous number of goals for a centre-back. He left the Bernabeu with a collection totalling 101 across all competitions, a return worthy of a decent striker.

The 40-year-old Spaniard was still playing at a high level until 2025, a testament to just how incredible he's been and continues to be after all these years. It's just a shame his time in Madrid didn't end on the most positive of notes.

A world-class player for Real Madrid and an equally good manager. In his playing days, 'Zizou' scored an incredible volley to win the 2001 Champions League final, and he then guided the club to a famous 'three-peat' in the competition from the dugout. The word 'legend' doesn't really do him justice.

Zidane was a ferocious engine in the middle of the park for the club and regularly bossed the opposition midfielders. They didn't stand a chance. He might have only spent five years playing at the Bernabeu, but his time as Real Madrid manager also added to his incredible legacy too.

Two Ballon d'Ors, 308 goals in 396 games, eight La Liga titles, five Pichichis and five European Cups; that's what Di Stefano achieved in his 11-year stint at Real Madrid. He also scored in every single one of the five European Cup finals he played in. They don't make them quite like the 'Blond Arrow' anymore.

He spent over a decade with Madrid, and the impact he had during that time cannot be overstated. It would take someone special to outshine his legacy at the club. Unfortunately, one of the very best players ever also happened to play for them at one point.

Alfredo Di Stefano's Real Madrid Statistics

Cristiano Ronaldo is Real Madrid's all-time record scorer with 450 goals, and he somehow achieved it in just 438 games. That return is absurd and will never be equalled by another player. Ronaldo also won four Champions Leagues at Real Madrid and scored 30 or more goals in every single season he was at the club. The 41-year-old really was a footballing cyborg in the Spanish capital.

He cost Madrid a world record transfer fee when he joined in 2009, and after nine incredible years, that saw him break all sorts of records and cement his status as one of the best players of all time, it's fair to say that he was still a bargain.

The water cycle is global, yet its accounting is not. Rain, rivers and underground water cross borders freely, but water use is reported by country. The budget for the world’s total usage is therefore only as reliable as the weakest report. When a country cannot measure usage, its water is lost from global accounting — and with it, any claim to a fair share.

#1310. 2026/27 Premier League Table Without 'VAR Errors'

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Video Assistant Referee (VAR) has its fair share of critics. Introduced to the Premier League at the start of the 2019/20 season, the technology was designed to help the on-pitch officials and ensure matches were officiated seamlessly and without controversy.

However, it has not had the impact that it was intended to have. If anything, the number of refereeing controversies has gone up, and many high-profile names, including Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney, have lost patience and want to see VAR scrapped.

But what would the 2026/27 Premier League table look like if every refereeing decision was correct? After every match day in England's top tier, Squawka asks their followers to vote on controversial VAR decisions and whether the right decision was made or not.

Using that data, they have created a Premier League table without VAR errors following matchday 9, and it makes for interesting reading.

The table has been compiled on the basis that penalties, should they have been awarded, would have been converted.

Sunderland have had a dismal start to the campaign. The Black Cats, who are competing in the Conference League after finishing seventh in 2025/26, are currently rock bottom of the Premier League having picked up five points from their opening nine games. They can't blame VAR for their troubles, either, as they would remain in the same position without its errors.

Crystal Palace would be second bottom, with Manchester United rounding out the relegation places. Nottingham Forest, who are currently 19th in the Premier League, would be two points better off and would be above Palace and United in the table had VAR been perfect.

Back in September, Forest and Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 at the City Ground. VAR is adjudged to have wrongly intervened to disallow Neco Williams' goal for the home side. The Premier League released a statement explaining the goal had been ruled out for handball, but many felt the footage was inconclusive and not clear and obvious. Had VAR made the right decision, Forest would have won 1-0.

Fulham and Coventry City will both remain in 15th and 16th. Neither have had a VAR error go for or against them so far this season.

Hull City have had a tremendous start, but they would be a point and three places worse off without VAR errors. Newcastle United would remain in 13th, with their points tally and goal difference unchanged.

Tottenham and Aston Villa are now both in the top half after overcoming poor starts. Both teams have benefited from VAR errors, though. Spurs would drop from ninth to 12th after getting a controversial point against Forest, which they wouldn't have done had Williams' goal been correctly given. Villa would also drop a spot.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (20-11)

Leeds United have had a decent start to the season under Daniel Farke, but it would have been even better without VAR errors. They are currently 12th, but would be two places better off in 10th if correct decisions were made.

Ipswich Town can also be happy with their start. They've picked up 11 points from their opening nine matches and are currently four points above the drop zone. Without VAR errors, they would actually be a whopping six places better off and comfortably in the top half.

Everton would remain in seventh, while Liverpool and Chelsea would drop a place to sixth and fifth respectively, with Brentford jumping above them into the top four.

Manchester City would be two points worse off and drop a place from second to third without VAR errors. They won 1-0 at Old Trafford thanks to Erling Haaland's winner. ProRef released a statement revealing that the goal should have been ruled out due to Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position. Without that goal, the match would've ended in a goalless draw and Brighton would be above them on goal difference as a result.

Arsenal have picked up 24 points from their opening nine matches, winning eight and losing one. They wouldn't have beaten Liverpool without VAR errors, though.

Liverpool felt aggrieved that they weren't given a penalty when Alexander Isak's shirt was tugged by Jurrien Timber in the box, preventing him from having a header at goal. If VAR had made the right decision, Liverpool would've been given a spot-kick, and it is assumed they would have scored and that the spoils would have been shared.

Despite that, Mikel Arteta's side would still be well clear at the top of the table without VAR errors.

#1308. Kobbie Mainoo is New Man Utd Leader Under Carrick, He's Undroppable

Manchester United snapped their nine game winless run with a comeback victory over AS Roma in the Champions League at Old Trafford on Tuesday night.

The Red Devils looked to be on the way to a tenth straight game without a win after falling 2-0 behind inside the opening 19 minutes against the Serie A outfit, thanks to goals from Mathias Soule and a Donyell Malen penalty.

But a resurgent performance in the second half saw Bruno Fernandes pull one back with a re-taken penalty, before Matheus Cunha scored twice to hand the team their first victory since a September win over Sabah.

United were forced to complete the comeback without star midfield signing Carlos Baleba, after the Cameroon international suffered a hamstring injury in the opening seconds of the second half.

It was the first time that Carrick had been able to partner him alongside Kobbie Mainoo this season, and the team struggled to deal with Roma's width on the counter-attack, while a number of individual errors caused them issues. But in the second half, when United needed something to get them going, there was one man to step up.

In recent history that man has always been Bruno Fernandes. The captain has regularly popped up with goals, assists, and influential performances to drag his team back from the despair of defeat. But against Roma, despite the Portuguese playmaker registering a goal and assist, there was another player who stepped up and took the bull by the horns.

Kobbie Mainoo had 97 touches of the ball, completed 85% of his passes, completed three of his four dribble attempts, carried the ball 32 times, made 12 recoveries, won seven ground duels, and turned in a magnificent performance when considering he was returning from injury, having been forced to miss the last four games.

It's not the first time the young midfielder has taken the game by the scruff of the neck and helped Man Utd get a positive result, and the fact he was the man chosen to address the media before the game suggests his standing in the dressing room is growing.

Speaking ahead of the game, he stated that he felt the team just needed one win to get back on track, and he helped to deliver it with an outstanding performance.

"I feel like our way to repay that is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it, and fight for us and fight for us as a team.

"It's been a tough season. We haven't had the results we wanted, but you know we need to look forward now. There are big, big games ahead, and I feel like we're one win away from changing that.

It's wild to think that 12 months ago there were conversations about Mainoo leaving the club because he couldn't get any minutes under Ruben Amorim, and the board were willing to sanction it.

Fast forward to now, and the 21-year-old is undoubtedly the first name on the team sheet for Carrick, and he is now growing into his role as a leader on and off the pitch.

The manager has shown that he isn't afraid to drop players, with Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez finding themselves on the bench recently, but Mainoo is someone who seems undroppable now. His influence and quality are unmatched in the squad, and it's no surprise that, in seven starts this season, United have only lost one, and that was the controversial defeat to Man City. Without him in the starting lineup, United have lost six times out of seven.

Man Utd are heading into a new era at Old Trafford, and whether it's Carrick or someone else in the dugout, Mainoo is the new leader and everything should be built around him.

Davinson Sanchez found himself in the middle of an on-pitch brawl on Tuesday as he and his Galatasaray team-mates confronted their Stuttgart counterparts.

#1304. White Card Was First Shown by Football Referee During Sporting vs Benfica

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Did you know that a white card was first shown during a match in 2023 between Portuguese rivals Sporting and Benfica?

Yellow and red cards have been part and parcel of football for decades now, so the sight of a white card looked incredibly bizarre to every football fan.

The new card was shown shortly before half-time of the women’s football fixture in Portugal. Benfica were 3-0 up when the ref pulled the white card out and brandished it in the same way a match official would a yellow or red card.

This was the first time a white card had ever been used, and it sparked plenty of confusion - and debate - at the time. Watch the footage below:

But what's the purpose of a white card in football, and when is it used? Well, in this specific scenario, it was reported that someone in the dugout had suddenly fallen ill towards the end of the first half. Medical staff from both sides subsequently rushed to the person’s aid.

Once the issue was dealt with, the referee then brandished the white card, much to the delight of fans inside the Estadio da Luz. Unlike yellow and red cards, which punish teams for breaking football’s rules, white cards are designed to recognise and praise clubs for fair play.

Part of a new initiative in Portugal at the time, the hope was that a white card would encourage ethical values in sport. On this particular occasion, the white card was shown in the direction of the medical staff, who were quick on the scene to treat the person in the dugout.

It sounds like a nice idea in principle, doesn’t it? The white card provides immediate recognition for a positive act during a football match.

The initiative was part of a series of new introductions in football, which also included concussion substitutions and longer stoppage time - as was witnessed during the 2022 World Cup finals in Qatar.

However, three years on and we're yet to see white cards become commonplace in football. While the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) implemented the white card across its domestic competitions, according to the Olympics' official website, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) are yet to formally introduce the card into the laws of the game.

“The aim of the card is to recognise, highlight and reward ethically relevant attitudes and behaviour of practitioners, coaches, managers, among other agents directly involved in the game, as well as spectators," Portugal's National Plan for Ethics in Sport (PNED) stated in 2023. There is currently no threshold for when a referee can issue a white card during a match.

Think you know everything about football? A question asked on The Chase about a strange rule could still catch you out

The white card isn't the only new card in football to create headlines in recent years. In early 2024, fans and pundits alike debated the pros and cons of a potential blue card, which would lead to a 10-minute suspension for players guilty of a cynical foul or for showing dissent towards a match official. Following a backlash, IFAB eventually dropped the plans as part of a trial into sin bins.

And in 2018, a green card experiment was conducted during the CONIFA World Football Cup - a tournament for non-FIFA affiliated international teams. A Padania player was shown a green card and ordered him to leave the pitch.

The idea of the green card, similar to the blue card, was that it would lead to a reduction in dissent shown towards officials. CONIFA rules stated that "a player who receives a green card must leave the field of play immediately, but can be replaced if his team have not used all of their substitutes. A player receiving a green card is not excluded from his team's next match."

"We'd really like to clamp down on the dissent problem. Football has a problem with the lack of respect for referees," tournament organiser Paul Watson said at the time. "That's not to say that isn't also the case in CONIFA games - the players in our tournament still have those traits.

"But it would be nice that, instead of it being ignored and therefore in a way condoned, it shouldn't necessarily cost someone their chance to play at this tournament, if they just lose their cool."

Meanwhile, a new purple card was trialled alongside a new blue card at the 2025 FIFA Under-20 World Cup. These Football Video Support (FVS) cards allow coaches to challenge decisions as an alternative to VAR.

#1303. Man Utd 's Matheus Cunha Has Saved Michael Carrick - He Should Repay Him

Matheus Cunha was the match-winner for Manchester United against Roma on Tuesday. The Brazilian scored a brace to help spearhead a sensational second-half comeback for the Reds, as they came from 2-0 down to beat the Italian side 3-2 on a historic night at Old Trafford.

Roma had got off to a flying start and went ahead through Matias Soule's 11th-minute strike. Donyell Malen then put Gian Piero Gasperini's side two-nil in front six minutes later, slotting home from the spot after Ayden Heaven handled the ball in the box.

Although United didn't provide an immediate response, they were much improved after half-time and pulled one back with Bruno Fernandes converting a penalty in the 57th minute.

That sparked life into the United faithful, but it took until the 82nd minute for the Reds to equalise. Cunha pounced on a defensive error from Roma before slamming the ball home from close range.

Cunha then scored his second and United's third two minutes later to complete the comeback. He got on the end of a terrific pass from Shea Lacey before drilling the ball in off the post.

Despite receiving a late red card for two quick-fire bookable offences - one of which was for jumping into the crowd to celebrate his winning goal - Cunha was United's standout performer.

The Brazilian has saved Michael Carrick, there is no doubt about that, and the United head coach should repay him with a consistent run in the side and be the club's first-choice left-winger.

Cunha ended his six-match goal drought with the brace against Roma, and it felt much-needed for the forward, who had faced some criticism from the United fans during his barren run.

But what Cunha has got is a natural goalscoring instinct that United do lack when he is not on the pitch. When he is confident, he is United's most dangerous attacker.

He showed what he is all about against Roma and can be lethal when given a chance inside the box. The ex-Wolves man, who joined United in a £62.5m deal, had four shots and scored two of them, with both excellent finishes in their own right, having kept his composure from close range and hammered one in from a tight angle.

As well as that, Cunha won United's penalty which sparked the comeback. He was fouled inside the box before Fernandes stepped up to convert at the second attempt.

Without Cunha, United would not have won the game and Carrick could well have been sacked, with Fabian Hurzeler not wanting the Man Utd job if that were to happen. The Reds were without a win in NINE going into the match against Roma and the pressure had been rising on the United boss. But Cunha's late double has appeared to have saved him.

Due to that and Cunha's impressive second-half performance, Carrick should give him a longer run in the team now and use him as his starting left-winger, even when Marcus Rashford is back.

Rashford has flattered to deceive since returning from his loan at Barcelona and Cunha has been in better form this season, despite his recent dip.

Cunha had started the opening six Premier League matches this season before dropping to the bench for the trip to Leeds United. He had been in and out of the side up until returning for the game against Chelsea on Saturday and then on Tuesday at home to Roma.

Four goals across all competitions for Cunha is United's joint-most alongside Bryan Mbeumo and more could follow if he produces the same level of performance as he did against Roma.

It wouldn't be a surprise if he follows that up against Aston Villa on Sunday, with United desperate for a result in the Premier League.

GMS senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs revealed in his exclusive newsletter that a deal was close.

"Barcelona have been credited with an interest, but Barcelona sporting director Deco told me several weeks ago at the Portugal Football Summit that they were not currently working on a deal.

"PSG have made a pitch, so have Bayern Munich, but JJ Gabriel has been training in Madrid, and the expectation is that he is now close to joining Jose Mourinho's side.

"Manchester United's perspective is that they haven't had any contact yet or formal communication with the camp of JJ Gabriel or Real Madrid.

"They will be entitled to some compensation, and it's also worth noting that as long as JJ Gabriel is registered at Manchester United, they will explore their legal options if a club comes in and says they have agreed a deal with the player, but there's a catch that works against Manchester United, and that is if JJ Gabriel and his family show a relocation to an EU country, the player has an EU passport, and there is a business with non-footballing income unrelated to the transfer and the player, then JJ Gabriel will have dispensation to cancel his registration.

"Manchester United will be entitled to compensation, or there is a chance to protect the club-to-club relationship that Real Madrid decide to negotiate with Manchester United and make it more amicable, and then that could allow Manchester United to make more money, but it looks like JJ Gabriel is going to leave Old Trafford and Real Madrid are now close to securing his signature."

#1298. Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. If the verdicts are upheld, of course, it wasn’t their penthouse and it wasn’t their caviar.

We got to live in a penthouse and eat caviar for 15 years and if we have to go back to a semi in the suburbs, well, fine.

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

#1297. Man United mock Roma with brutal tweet after comeback victory

Manchester United enjoyed their comeback win against Roma on and off the field, mocking the Giallorossi with a brutal tweet at full-time.

Roma wasted a two-goal lead at Old Trafford last night: they scored twice in the opening 17 minutes but conceded three times in the second half, falling to a 3-2 loss.

Manchester United hadn’t won a game since September, while Roma had lost only once across all competitions before last night’s meeting.

Ironically, Roma had lost to Real Madrid in a similar fashion in October, falling 4-3 at the Stadio Olimpico and conceding three goals in the dying minutes.

Manchester United kept celebrating on and off the pitch, taking to X, formerly Twitter, to share a series of cheeky posts after their victory.

One post featured the stadium screens displaying the results of previous Champions League encounters with Roma, alongside last night’s triumph. The scoreboard highlighted their emphatic 7-1 victory in April 2007 and the 6-2 win in 2021.

Manchester United captioned the image with a simple but fitting message: “Absolute Cinema.”

#1296. The Dominik Szoboszlai dilemma: One of Europe's best midfielders who Liverpool must build around? Or a square peg who they play better without? This is what Andoni Iraola should do

Published: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026

The folks in Liverpool’s commercial team devoted a fair portion of last season chasing after Dominik Szoboszlai.

As the club's player of the month more often than not, the Hungarian was obliged to fulfil a swathe of sponsorship duties and, like for many defenders last season, tying down Szoboszlai was not always easy. But he always completed these extracurricular activities, and was rewarded with a bumper new contract.

The midfielder was the standard-setter in pre-season and made vice-captain, with an eye on becoming the next man to wear the armband permanently when Virgil van Dijk eventually leaves. Szoboszlai’s role as protagonist continued in Andoni Iraola’s first competitive match with a last-gasp thunderous strike at Newcastle. Everything at Liverpool, it seemed, revolved around this handsome, chiseled star with a swagger.

Fast forward two months, however, and that's no longer the case. Szoboszlai has gone from first name on the teamsheet to having to fight for a starting spot. For some fans, he has become the scapegoat.

That seems wholly unfair but they point to the fact his half an hour from the bench against Arsenal coincided with Liverpool ceding control, balance and threat. Before that, Szoboszlai had missed four-and-a-half games – he went off injured early in a win at Brentford – and the Reds won all of them.

So, are Liverpool really better without the Hungarian? Let’s analyse both sides of the argument.

Would Andoni Iraola (right) really be better off without Dominik Szoboszlai (right)?

FOR: Drop him, he doesn’t fit Iraola’s system

The case against Szoboszlai revolves around balance, control and space.

Is it a coincidence that Florian Wirtz’s best run in a Liverpool shirt came in the last month, when the German had two midfielders behind him who were happy to do the defensive dirty work?

With both Szoboszlai and Wirtz in the side, it feels like the pair get in each other’s way and try to occupy the same positions, and Liverpool in turn are vulnerable to the counter-attack.

Alexis Mac Allister is enjoying his best form in well over a year and likes to arrive late into the box, but he cannot do this with Szoboszlai next to him as it leaves his team too exposed going the other way.

Young Trey Nyoni is a classy midfielder who thrives at dropping deep to start attacks and bait opposition presses. The 19-year-old is happy to sit back and allow those in front of him to thrive, such as Mac Allister playing a box-to-box role.

When Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled.

When Trey Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled

Szoboszlai is arrogant but has every right to be.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. A goal threat with one of the fiercest long shots in the game, with dead-ball precision, he is every bit the player Liverpool thought they were buying from RB Leipzig in 2023.

The midfielder has an engine akin to Declan Rice and is tireless in his work rate.

Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him. As shown last term, he can win matches on his own. Despite his recent lay-off, he is barely injured and is a standard-bearer on the training pitch.

Iraola’s system is a 4-2-3-1 on paper but the Basque wants a bit of everything from his midfield: one No6, one No8 and one No10. Szoboszlai can play each of those roles. He has a tattoo of a Steven Gerrard quote and is the closest player to the former skipper that Anfield has seen since.

Internally, Liverpool believe Szoboszlai’s best years are ahead of him. In signing him up to a five-year deal at the end of last season – a process led by former sporting director Richard Hughes with the player’s agent Matyas Esterhazy – the Reds hierarchy were glad to stave off any future approaches from the likes of Real Madrid.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him

There are four solutions, two of which are outlined above: drop him and have a more balanced midfield or play him and benefit from his goal-scoring and creative powers, plus leadership and relentless running.

Another option may not be popular but there is a Wirtz-shaped elephant in the room. Does Iraola bench Wirtz and play Szoboszlai as the No10?

He’d have fewer defensive duties so the control and balance remains, but the Hungarian would pop up in dangerous areas to cause issues. Wirtz is a creative wizard when on form but how many times does he pass up an opportunity to shoot? Szoboszlai would already be wheeling away in celebration by the time Wirtz has made his mind up on what to do with an attack.

And then there is the compromise of Szoboszlai at right back. The player himself does not like it as he feels less important in that position, but it solves a lot of issues including all the aforementioned balance and control quirks. It also adds one thing that is bothering Iraola – creativity and attacking verve from right back.

The downside of this is Liverpool would lose the defensive acumen and physicality of aerial presence of Ronald Araujo, who is currently enjoying cult hero status at right back.

Szoboszlai is a strong right back but does not like playing there as he believes he has less influence on the game

The best teams build around the best players. There are always similar debates around Erling Haaland at Manchester City and anyone who argues the case to drop him is made to look silly.

So I will say the same about Szoboszlai. It is on Iraola to make it work. Most managers would kill for a depth of midfield talent like he has. Why not play him at right back? It solves multiple issues at once and Liverpool can finally replace the creativity Trent Alexander-Arnold used to bring from that role.

If Liverpool are seeing a game out, they can push Szoboszlai to the No 10, sub off Wirtz and bring on a true defender to help the physical battle.

Liverpool will be reunited with an old friend on Wednesday – and former cult hero Dirk Kuyt is relishing the chance to beat his old team.

Kuyt, played 285 times for the Reds between 2006 and 2012, scoring 71 times – and will face his old team for the first time on Wednesday as manager of Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The Dutchman took over last week after a spell as assistant manager and said: ‘As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me.

‘It will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important – to show the fans who deserve much more.

‘If we show up tomorrow with good energy, with passion and there to play, it can be a very special night.

‘Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce. If the fans show up, I think Europe will see how big this fan base is.’

Liverpool have happy memories in Istanbul having won this competition here in 2005 – though they lost twice to Galatasaray in Turkey last season, in the league phase and then last-16.

Fenerbahce play on the Asian side of the city and have familiar faces such as Romelu Lukaku, N'Golo Kante, Ederson, Nathan Ake and Mason Greenwood.

Liverpool will be without midfielder Ryan Gravenberch, who has a heel problem.

Boss Andoni Iraola said he liked a lot of the performance against Arsenal on Sunday but his side still need to improve.

‘It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day,’ he said. ‘I liked a lot of things but we still need to improve, especially attacking the box.'
